newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says member states may tax interest free loans.
newsitem.headline: Court says member states may tax interest free loans.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday subsidiaries receiving interest free loans from their parent company may be taxed on interest saved, under Community rules on indirect taxes on raising capital.
The court decided the same directive did not preclude member states from taxing parent companies which gave interest free loans to subsidiaries.

"It is clear ... the directive is intended to abolish indirect taxes other than capital duty which possess the same characteristics as capital duty itself ... the harmonization does not extend to direct taxes, such as company income tax, which are a matter for the member states themselves," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the text: Danish)
"Raising of capital - Capital duty - Interest free loan granted by a parent company to its subsidiary - Company income tax"
Reference from the Ostre Landsret (Denmark) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
on the interpretation of articles 4(2)(b) and 10 of Council directive 69/335/EEC of 17 July 1969 concerning indirect taxes on the raising of capital (OJ, English Special Edition, 1969 (II), p. 412)

1. Article 4(2)(b)of Council directive 69/335/EEC of 17 July 1969 concerning indirect taxes on the raising of capital must be interpreted as applying, where a company benefits from an interest-free loan, to the amount of interest saved.

2. Article 10 of directive 69/335/EEC does not preclude the levying of income tax on a parent company which has granted an interest-free loan to one of its subsidiaries, on the basis of interest fixed after the event.
